questions.question: What does IOC stand for in threat intelligence?
options: Internal Operations Center
Indicator of Compromise
Index of Criticality
Inventory of Components
questions.explanation: An Indicator of Compromise is an artifact (IP, domain, file hash, etc.) associated with malicious activity, used to detect or correlate threats against your assets.

questions.question: Why correlate ASM findings with threat intelligence feeds?
options: To make the dataset larger
To prioritize exposures based on real threat context, such as actively exploited CVEs affecting your discovered services
Because ASM data is useless on its own
To replace vulnerability scanning entirely
questions.explanation: An exposed service running software with an actively exploited CVE matters far more than one with no known threat activity. Threat context turns an asset inventory into a prioritized risk picture.

questions.question: Which inputs typically feed a risk prioritization score for an ASM finding?
options: Only the CVSS score of any associated CVE
Asset exposure, threat context, and business criticality combined
The alphabetical position of the hostname
The age of the domain registration
questions.explanation: Good prioritization blends how exposed the asset is, whether threats actively target it, and how much the business depends on it — not just a raw severity number.

questions.question: Why must threat data be parsed and normalized before correlation?
options: Threat feeds arrive in different formats and schemas, and correlation requires a common structure
Normalization makes the data legally usable
Raw threat data is always encrypted
To reduce storage costs
questions.explanation: Feeds vary wildly — JSON APIs, CSV lists, STIX bundles. Normalizing them into a consistent internal format is what makes automated matching against your asset data possible.

questions.question: Which are typical examples of threat intelligence sources for ASM?
options: CVE databases, IOC feeds, and breach/credential-leak data
Marketing analytics platforms
Server uptime dashboards
Code style linters
questions.explanation: ASM programs commonly integrate CVE/vulnerability feeds, IOC lists, and leaked-credential or breach data to enrich and prioritize what discovery has found.
